maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT

speechtext:
Hon. J. A. ROBB (Minister of Trade and Commerce) moved the second reading of Bill No. 21, to amend the Trade Mark and Design Act.
Motion agreed to, bill read the second time and the House went into committee thereon, Mr. Marcil in the chair.
On section 1-Act amended so that Part II, Industrial Designs, will apply to designs of non-residents, etc.:

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The present act allows only residents of Canada to register industrial designs and trade marks. There is no good reason why that distinction should exist. Indeed that was recognized by the previous government and a bill was first brought in in
1920 to remove this distinction. For some reason or other that bill was dropped, but in 1921 another bill was brought in for the same purpose. From the record it appears that in connection with both the bill of 1920 and the bill of 1921 the Canadian manufacturers were consulted and approved of the proposed changes, but in 1921 when the bill was up for its second reading two sections of the Canadian Manufacturers' Association expressed some doubt to the government as to the regulations, and the bill was withdrawn. We are bringing in this bill at this time to make some corrections, believing that it is in the general interests of Canada. It is really along very similar lines to the Copyright Act which we were dealing with to-night, and the Patent Act which we passed a few days ago. If we are going to keep goods out of Canada the right method of doing it is through the custom house, and we now propose to remove the restrictions that exist in the Trade Mark and Design Act and bring that act into line with the Copyright Act and the Patent Act, so that generally all these goods will come under the Berne convention. The advantages of working under that convention are that Canadia'ns taking out patents in other countries will be protected in those countries. It is also of some material advantage, I submit, to the people of our own country that we should not restrict the registry of trade marks and designs to our own people here. It is an advantage to them to be able to register their trade marks and designs abroad. Let me give my hon. friends an illustration of how it might be of material advantage to Canada. Suppose that a co-operative association dealing in butter establishes as their design a clover leaf or maple leaf. Now unless we so amend our legislation as to enable a Canadian to register that trade mark in other countries, after his business has been built up some person might appropriate that design, as happened recently down in Brazil where a very valuable trade mark on fish was appropriated. Those generally are the reasons for presenting these slight amendments to the bill.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: I suppose that the American act is free of these words?

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: Canadians can now register in the United States.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: This does not affect our business in the United States at all?

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext:
No. It will affect it in Russia, China, and a number of the South American republics.

Trade Mark and Design Act

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: I was interested in what my hon. friend said. When we were discussing the Patent Act he said that we had an arrangement whereby we kept goods out by the Patent Act while the Americans did it through their high tariff, and he said the same thing in connection with the Copyright Act. I would ask the minister now that these barriers are being taken down, whether he does not think that the customs should be rearranged.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: I will go into that with my hon.' friend later.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: But we are considering the bill now. The book of annual statistics for the United States shows for the last accounting year a per capita purchasing ratio or figure of $131.66 for Canada and $24 for the United States. Apparently the high tariff in the United States is much more effective than the Canadian low tariff plus these patent and copyrights acts to which my hon. friend has referred. Does he think that abnormality should be removed?

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is another question.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: We are considering now one of the safeguards and I do not know why we should not have a little frankness on the question. Why not? It is desirable, is it not, that we should know exactly what we are doing and I am giving the minister the latest figures and asking him for his view? Surely the point I am urging has something to do with this question.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: My hon. friend will observe there is a reciprocal advantage in removing this because of the benefit that our trade marks and designs will enjoy in some other country.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: Apparently the minister does not want to discuss the business of his own department.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: Not at this late hour.

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: I can well understand that desire.

Section agreed to.
On section 2-Conditions of registration:

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext: This amendment is necessary under the terms of the International convention and to make this legislation conform to the Patent Act in that regard.

Section agreed to.
On section 3-Filing of application already filed in another country.
(Mr. Robb.]

maintopic: TRADE MARK AND DESIGN ACT AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Copies of this bill when printed and of the Patent Act were sent over to the British authorities. We have not advanced the bill furthe. because some days ago we received a cable from them requesting that certain slight amendments be made so thao the bill might very properly conform to the regulations. To meet the British government's requirements I propose to move the following.
That clause 3 of bill No. 21 be amended by adding an "s" to the word "section" in the first line and substituting for the word "is the word "are" in said line and by adding to said clause the following:
50. Any trade mark the proprietor of which is an association the existence of which is not contrary to the law of the country to which such association belongs, even if such association does not possess an industrial or commercial establishment may be registered under this act upon compliance with the requirements thereof and on such particular conditions as may be established by regulations to be made by the minister with the approval of the Governor in Council.
The object is to put co-operative associations on the same basis as incorporated companies or individuals.
